verdict.root_cause: paymentservice is not failing to serve payments — it is failing to be observed. Five minutes before the 23:05 alert, platform-automation set OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT to http://127.0.0.1:4317, a loopback address with no collector behind it, and unlike four earlier set/revert pairs in the same window this one was never reverted and was in effect at onset [tr_3fc206e3cba2]. The value itself names a wrong address and that wrongness is the failure: span-derived calls_total for paymentservice returns no samples at all [tr_327aa30e6511], while the service's own logs show charge/completion pairs continuing sub-millisecond across 23:04–23:06 with no errors [tr_fc89f8e7fd07] and caller checkoutservice shows error ratio below baseline with no change point at 23:05 [tr_ec4f6e6c8903]. Fix is reverting the endpoint to the real collector and stopping the automation flap.
verdict.reasoning: Logs rule out paymentservice as an error origin, rule out downstream timeouts, and rule out a crash or traffic stop [tr_fc89f8e7fd07]; checkoutservice metrics rule out it being the origin or deviating at 23:05 [tr_ec4f6e6c8903]. So no request-path failure is visible anywhere in the blast radius. The one demonstrably broken thing is paymentservice's telemetry path [tr_327aa30e6511], and the change log supplies a mechanism with matching timing and no revert [tr_3fc206e3cba2]. Not bad_deploy: no deploy or image entries exist in the window. Not dependency_latency: charges complete in about a millisecond.
open_questions: What signal actually fired the 23:05 alert? Neither metrics nor logs show a symptom at that timestamp, and no user-facing impact evidence exists.
The metrics baseline (20:05–23:05) is also empty, but the loopback value was only re-applied at 22:59 — so the missing series predates this change and is not fully explained by it.

Label mismatch is unresolved: logs use service="payment-service", the metric query uses service_name="paymentservice". If the selector is simply wrong, the empty result is a query artifact and this verdict weakens.

alternatives.root_cause: The paymentservice metric series never existed under the queried label, so the 'outage' is a broken query/observability pipeline unrelated to the 22:59 change.
alternatives.why_not: Consistent with the empty baseline, but leaves the un-reverted loopback endpoint five minutes before onset as an unexplained coincidence; also predicts no incident at all.

alternatives.root_cause: A real degradation exists in an unmeasured downstream of paymentservice, crossed by the two unmeasured triage edges and never probed.
alternatives.why_not: Payment logs show charges completing within about a millisecond with no timeout or dependency-failure lines across the onset period [tr_fc89f8e7fd07].

proposal.expected_effect: No action proposed. The verdict is medium-confidence and its central observation — an empty calls_total series for paymentservice [tr_327aa30e6511] — is unresolved between two explanations: the loopback exporter endpoint, or a label mismatch (logs use service="payment-service", the query uses service_name="paymentservice"). The empty baseline covers 20:05–23:05 while the loopback value was only re-applied at 22:59 [tr_3fc206e3cba2], so the gap predates the change and is not explained by it. Cheap next step before any action: re-run the metric query with service_name="payment-service" and list actual label values on calls_total. If data appears, the verdict collapses to a query artifact and no remediation is warranted.
proposal.if_wrong: If the corrected-label query is still empty and paymentservice spans are genuinely absent, then revert_config on paymentservice becomes the right proposal and this abstention delayed a fix by one query. Cost of that delay is low: logs show charges completing sub-millisecond with no errors across 23:04–23:06 [tr_fc89f8e7fd07], so no user-facing impact is accruing.
proposal.risk: Abstaining leaves the loopback endpoint in place, so paymentservice traces stay unexported and the service remains unobservable in the metrics path. It also leaves the platform-automation flap loop running. The counter-risk of acting is that revert_config recreates the container of a service currently serving real payments cleanly, dropping in-flight charges for an observability-only defect, and platform-automation has re-applied this variable after four prior reverts — so the fix would likely be undone within minutes anyway.
proposal.blast_radius: No change made, so nobody sees anything new. Had the revert run, checkoutservice would see connection resets during the recreate and frontend the same blip one hop further out; the collector at the restored address would begin receiving paymentservice traffic.

triage_judgement.reasoning: A single critical alert on paymentservice sits upstream of checkout and frontend, so it cannot be dismissed as a working world. No open incidents to attribute it to, and the alert alone does not indicate a fault class.
